- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.53) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.27) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.27–0.53), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
- If true price exceeds forecast by >2% for 2+ consecutive days, model is likely underestimating; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- In high-sentiment periods (e.g., 0.53+ for 3+ days), model often fails to capture mean reversion; reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day until sentiment drops below 0.40.
